title: Micro-handoff signals and declarative prefetch PRD
summary: Sketch PRD for a lightweight streaming handshake that surfaces micro-handoff signals and a declarative prefetch manifest to improve latency for tool-calling and progressive structured enrichment while keeping SDK surface minimal.
goals: (1) Reduce median tail latency for first tool result by enabling client-declared prefetch intent and server-side micro-handoff signals. (2) Provide a minimal SDK ergonomics layer so product teams can opt-in with a single-line toggle. (3) Ensure structured-output integrity across partial/commit frames and fallbacks.
non_goals: This doc does not design a new transport (we keep HTTP/streaming SSE & websockets). It does not replace full session semantics or storage models for long-term resume. No changes to billing model in this iteration.
problem_statement: Many integrations suffer from long first-tool latencies because clients cannot express intent early enough and servers cannot safely pre-warm tool runtimes without explicit, low-cost signals. Current streaming frames conflate model output with tool lifecycle metadata, leading to brittle SDK handling and developer confusion when partial structured outputs arrive and later change. We need a small handshake vocabulary + declarative prefetch manifest that reduces cold tool latency and clarifies commit semantics while remaining simple for SDK authors.
success_metrics: - 30% reduction in P95 latency for first tool-response in benchmarks (sample workloads: retrieval-then-lookup, code-exec toollets). - <1% client-side parsing errors when partial structured frames are emitted. - Adoption: >= 20 internal experimental integrations in 8 weeks.
constraints: - Must work with existing streaming API and typed frames (no new long-lived socket required). - Minimal changes to server billing and routing. - SDK additions must be opt-in and small (<150 lines user-facing). - Backwards compatible: older clients should ignore new signals safely.
proposal_overview: Introduce a micro-handoff handshake layer composed of three things: (A) a lightweight declarative prefetch manifest embedded in the initial request; (B) a set of compact server-to-client micro-signals emitted as special stream frames (prefetch-ack, tool-reserve, tool-ready, partial-commit, final-commit); (C) a minimal SDK facade that exposes prefetch intents, a toollet lifecycle callback, and structured-output commit events.
prefetch_manifest_spec: - format: small JSON list (string tokens) describing tool intents and optional hints (e.g., ['vector-search:top-k=3', 'runner:lang=python,min-memory=512MB']). - placed in request metadata as header X-RW-PREFETCH or first body frame for streaming calls. - server can use manifest to warm tool execution pools or prioritize routing to nodes with cached artifacts. - manifest has TTL and priority: TTL default 5s for ephemeral prefetch, priority levels (low/normal/high).
micro_handoff_signals: 1) prefetch-ack: server acknowledges manifest and returns best-effort estimated warm-up (ms). 2) tool-reserve: server indicates reserved runtime instance id (opaque token) for a named tool. 3) tool-ready: tool runtime is ready to accept input; attached with ETA. 4) partial-commit: partial structured output that should be treated as a checkpoint; may be mutated later unless labeled 'immutable'. 5) final-commit: final structured artifact; client may commit to downstream processing. Signals are emitted as named stream frames with concise payloads (string/kv) to minimize parsing cost.
sdk_surface_proposal: - opt-in flag: ClientOptions.prefetch = true | manifest. - callback: onToolSignal(toolName, signalType, metadata). - convenience: waitFor(toolName, timeoutMs) -> resolves when tool-ready or rejects. - handlers for partialCommit/finalCommit: registerCommitCallback(routeId, cb). - lightweight local simulator: SDK exposes a validateManifest(manifest) method to lint hints before sending. - fallthrough: SDK must surface graceful degradation when no prefetch-ack or tool-ready arrives in TTL.
example_request_flow: 1) Client sends streaming call with X-RW-PREFETCH header: ['vector-search:top-k=3','code-runner:lang=python']. 2) Server emits prefetch-ack(frame) with estimated warm time 120ms. 3) Server emits tool-reserve for 'vector-search' with token T-42. 4) Model emits a generated tool-call frame referencing T-42. 5) Server emits tool-ready for 'vector-search' before routing the call to the warmed instance. 6) Client receives partial-commit frames (structured JSON as text) and waits for final-commit. 7) SDK invokes commit callback when final-commit arrives.
observability_and_telemetry: Server emits telemetry keys for each signal: r.prefetch.ack.latency_ms, r.tool.reserve.count, r.tool.ready.time_ms, r.partial.commit.count, r.commit.latency_ms. SDK surfaces local metrics for missed-prefetch(yes/no), waitFor-timeouts, and parse-errors. Add a per-request trace id to connect model frames, tool signals, and infrastructure traces in the Console.
failure_modes_and_fallbacks: - No prefetch ack: proceed normally; SDK treats prefetch as hint only. - Reserve but no ready: reserve token expires; routing falls back to on-demand tool execution. - Partial-commit mutated: server marks frames with 'mutable=true' and attaches version. SDK must avoid acting on mutable partials until final-commit. - Tool error: emit tool-error signal with recoverability flag (retryable/non-retryable) and suggested backoff.
security_and_privacy: - Prefetch manifest can include opaque keys but must not contain PII. - Tool-reserve tokens are short-lived and scoped to the request. - All signals go over the authenticated streaming channel and inherit request-level access controls.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (lab): implement feature flag + internal SDK hook; run 10 internal experiments (2 weeks). Phase 2 (canary): enable on 5% of hosted traffic for selected customer integrations (4 weeks). Phase 3 (beta): public opt-in in SDKs, enable Console tracing views (6 weeks). Phase 4 (GA): on by default with telemetry and migration guide (8–12 weeks).
compatibility_guidance: Older clients: unknown frames ignored. New servers: when sending tool-ready/reserve, also include legacy-friendly tool-call frames so older clients receive the same functional payload. SDKs should default to no-op for prefetch until opt-in.
developer_diagnostics_playbook: - If no tool-ready observed: check r.tool.ready.time_ms and reserve token allocation logs. - High partial-commit mutation rate: inspect model rollout/regression and structured output schema mismatches. - Client parse error: provide sample failing frame in Console with raw bytes and suggested schema.
open_questions: - Should manifest hints be rate-limited per account to avoid excessive warm-ups? - How to standardize hint qualifiers (min-memory vs memory-class)? - Should Reserve tokens be exposed to customers for advanced routing? - Billing: do we charge for warm-up reservations? (proposal: no charge for ephemeral warm-ups <200ms)
next_steps: (1) Engineering: prototype server frame emitter and short-lived reserve tokens (owner: Miguel). (2) SDK: add minimal callbacks and manifest validator in JS/TS + Python (owner: Claire). (3) Product: prepare internal experiment matrix and select test integrations (owner: Asha). (4) Observability: add telemetry keys and Console trace mapping (owner: SRE).
notes_to_self: Keep the SDK surface intentionally tiny. The primary win is latency reduction for first tool-result; don't over-index on rich manifests in this phase. Document a small list of canonical hint tokens to avoid fragmentation.
acceptance_criteria: - Prototype demonstrates >=20% median latency improvement on our benchmark harness for cold toollets. - SDKs pass integration tests with simulated partial/final commit semantics. - Console shows correlated traces for signals in canary traffic.
final_notes: This PRD is intentionally a sketch to bootstrap experiments. The next revision will include precise wire-format examples and an opt-in header schema that passes security review.
